# Draft:Traditional Khmer massage

----
Traditional Khmer massage
Traditional Khmer massage is a form of traditional manual therapy originating in Cambodia. It is associated with Cambodian traditional healing practices that combine physical manipulation, pressure techniques, assisted stretching, and elements of traditional medicine. The practice forms part of Cambodia's broader traditional health knowledge, which historically included herbal medicine, spiritual healing, and preventative body care.
Traditional Khmer massage is practiced in Cambodia in wellness settings, traditional healing environments, and hospitality contexts. Techniques are generally intended to promote relaxation, circulation, and general physical well-being.
History
The historical development of traditional Khmer massage is often linked to the broader medical and wellness knowledge of the Angkor period (9th to 15th centuries). Archaeological evidence from temple bas-reliefs at Angkor depicts scenes of daily life, ritual practices, and healthcare-related activities, reflecting the importance of health and body care in Khmer society.
Traditional Cambodian healing knowledge developed through a combination of indigenous healing traditions, cultural exchange with Indian medical systems including Ayurvedic influence, and Buddhist monastic healthcare practices.
Following the decline of the Angkor Empire, traditional healing knowledge was largely transmitted orally through local healers, families, and monastic communities rather than formal written medical systems.
During the 20th century, periods of conflict and social disruption contributed to the decline of many traditional knowledge systems in Cambodia. In recent decades, cultural organizations and researchers have shown increased interest in documenting and preserving traditional Cambodian healing practices.
Techniques
Traditional Khmer massage techniques may include rhythmic pressure, assisted stretching, and manual manipulation of muscle groups and soft tissue areas. Techniques commonly involve the use of thumbs, palms, forearms, and elbows to apply pressure.
Historically, some traditional techniques were performed without oils, although modern variations may incorporate oils depending on therapeutic or spa contexts.
Regional context
Traditional Khmer massage exists alongside other Southeast Asian massage traditions. Many regional massage systems share historical influences from Indian medical traditions and long-term cultural exchange across mainland Southeast Asia. However, local techniques, terminology, and treatment philosophies vary by region and cultural context.
Cultural significance
Traditional massage is considered part of Cambodia's traditional knowledge relating to health, wellness, and traditional medicine. It reflects historical Khmer approaches to physical care, natural medicine, and holistic well-being.
Efforts to preserve traditional knowledge have increased as part of broader cultural heritage preservation initiatives in Cambodia.
